transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-18 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Location: Zoom
Redwood owner: Avery Chen
Redwood attendees: Avery Chen (AE), Diego Ramos (SE)
Customer: Cobalt Health Systems — Maya Patel (Head of Security), Jordan Lee (Procurement), Samir Gupta (Platform Eng)

Summary:
Quick preflight between procurement, security and Redwood SE to align on MSA/DPA redlines, SSO and KMS integration expectations, and to sync on pricing gating items before formal procurement approval. Agreed actions around doc handoffs and scheduling a Private VPC demo + latency sampling.

Topics:
- MSA redline status and which clauses are blockers
- SSO (SAML) integration flows, metadata, and IdP discovery
- KMS / key management options (Redwood-managed vs customer KMS/HSM)
- Data residency / ingress/egress fees and pricing clarifications
- Pilot timeline and technical benchmark plan

Action items (captured verbally in call — also in metadata): see action_items list.

Transcript:
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we've got about 45 minutes, we wanted to make sure we hit the legal redlines, SSO/KMS integration, and then the technical scoping for a pilot.
[00:18] Maya Patel: Yep thanks, time's good. I just want to be clear on two things up front — one is whether Redwood supports bringing our own KMS and second is the SSO experience for our ops team.
[00:30] Diego Ramos: Totally, and we'll cover both. Quick note — apologies if the auto-transcript does weird things with acronyms, sometimes it turns K-V cash or K-V cache or V-P-C, so please bear with it.
[00:44] Jordan Lee: (laughs) that happened to our last vendor call, so I feel you. From procurement side I only need to know which clauses are go/no-go for finance — e.g., liability caps, data residency, and escrow.
[01:05] Avery Chen: Great, on MSA we're tracking the list you sent. High level: liability cap ask is noted, DPA changes around breach notification windows we're okay to accept with some language tweaks. There are two exception asks you flagged that our legal team wants to discuss — one around export controls and one around indemnity flow for third-party data processors.
[01:30] Maya Patel: Export controls is non-negotiable for us, we need explicit handling in the MSA and DPA. Indemnity we can be pragmatic on — but we need clear flow when downstream processors are involved.
[01:44] Avery Chen: Understood. We'll send a redline summary with proposed language tomorrow.
[01:50] Samir Gupta: On KMS, our preference is customer-managed keys in an HSM or cloud KMS. We need to ensure Redwood never has access to plaintext keys and that key rotation/trust boundary is enforced.
[02:10] Diego Ramos: We support both patterns — Redwood-managed for hosted customers and BYOK for Private deployments. For BYOK in Private mode we can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and a handful of HSM partners. There are a few implementation caveats — for example, the KV cache eviction patterns mean you need a short-lived encryption token for the runtime in some cases.
[02:35] Maya Patel: Short-lived token — can you expand? Our security team wants to ensure there are no long-lived credentials that could be exfiltrated.
[02:44] Diego Ramos: Sure. At runtime we obtain ephemeral wrapping keys from your KMS to encrypt model artifact caches — those tokens are scoped and rotated. The implementation depends on whether you're running Private (VPC) or Dedicated. In Private, the control plane is customer-managed so we never store keys. In Hosted, we can offer customer-side wrapping, but some customers prefer bringing keys.
[03:12] Jordan Lee: So practically, for procurement, does that change pricing or add an integration fee? We need to feed that into the approval packet.
[03:22] Avery Chen: Good question. BYOK for Private typically sits in our Private pricing band — there's a fixed onboarding fee for the initial integration plus a small monthly management premium if we manage the rotation automation. If you do everything in your VPC and manage rotation it reduces the integration fee. We'll put numbers in the follow up.
[03:40] Maya Patel: Also we have an internal policy around SSO — must be SAML 2.0, support automated provisioning (SCIM is preferred), and SSO sessions need to honor our session timeout policies.
[03:55] Diego Ramos: We support SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning. There is a standard SSO integration doc we can share — it lists required endpoints and metadata. For provisioning we support user attribute mapping and role-based provisioning.
[04:14] Samir Gupta: Any caveats about service accounts? We want a service account with limited permissions for telemetry ingestion only, not admin.
[04:24] Diego Ramos: Yep we have a pattern for non-admin service accounts and can scope tokens to telemetry scopes only. It shows up as a separate role in the provisioning doc.
[04:34] Jordan Lee: Back to MSA — Maya, aside from export controls, are there any SLA targets that are absolute requirements?
[04:41] Maya Patel: We need 99.9% availability SLA for the inference endpoint if we go to production, and a runbook for incident response including post-incident report within 72 hours.
[04:54] Avery Chen: Our Dedicated & Private tiers can commit to 99.9% and above; hosted tier is different. We'll confirm the language and include the incident RRT and postmortem timelines.
[05:08] Maya Patel: Cool. Also curious about EU data residency — some of our PHI-adjacent telemetry needs to stay in EU.
[05:16] Diego Ramos: We have region pinning for model serving, you can pin to eu-west and we can confirm logs and metrics residency as part of the DPA. There's usual caveat around backups and snapshotting — we'll note that.
[05:31] Samir Gupta: For the pilot, I propose a short smoke test: 1) basic inference correctness, 2) latency sampling at 128 tokens and 512 tokens, and 3) validate KMS key wrapping flows. Can Redwood provide a sampling plan?
[05:44] Diego Ramos: Yes we'll propose a 30–60 minute benchmark runbook. We'll instrument token-level latency and cold-starts; for 512 tokens we expect tails, but we'll show mitigations like pre-warming and prefix caching.
[06:02] Jordan Lee: On pricing objections — finance flagged per-token pricing unpredictability. They'd like a predictable cap or committed usage discount.
[06:12] Avery Chen: We have options — committed monthly reserved capacity (Dedicated) gives fixed cost per unit and predictable throughput. For hosted there's a committed spend discount, and for pilot we can provide a short fixed-price evaluation window to limit surprise spend.
[06:29] Maya Patel: That helps. Procurement also needs billing contact and a draft statement of work.
[06:35] Avery Chen: We'll include a skeleton SOW and billing contact in the follow up.
[06:41] (brief crosstalk)
[06:45] Maya Patel: One more security question — audit logs retention. We need 12-month retention for audit logs with role-level access and immutable storage.
[06:55] Diego Ramos: We can configure log retention and export to your SIEM. For Private we can push logs into your S3 with lifecycle policies; for hosted we have configurable retention tiers. Immutable storage can be arranged via write-once buckets or integration with your archive process.
[07:12] Samir Gupta: Great. Do you support SAML metadata exchange automatically via enterprise connector, or is it manual?
[07:20] Diego Ramos: We support automatic metadata fetch for some IdPs, but we also accept manual metadata upload. SCIM provisioning tends to be manual-to-automated depending on the IdP.
[07:33] Jordan Lee: Alright procurement note— timeline-wise, our vendor committee meets next Thursday; I need the MSA redline summary + pricing by Tuesday COB to include it.
[07:42] Avery Chen: Understood — we'll aim to deliver the redline summary and pricing sheet by 2026-02-20 EOD.
[07:50] Maya Patel: For the KMS diagram, Samir will export an architecture — Samir, can you do that by Monday?
[07:56] Samir Gupta: Yeah I'll have a topology + key rotation policy by 2026-02-23. Monday is a bit tight; I'll target Tuesday but will try for Monday.
[08:06] Diego Ramos: I'll prepare the Private deployment checklist and a short sampling plan — will share by 2026-02-21.
[08:12] (silence, paper rustle)
[08:20] Maya Patel: One small point — are there any data escrow or escrow pricing clauses we need to pre-discuss? Our legal sometimes asks for escrow in case of insolvency.
[08:31] Avery Chen: We have an escrow offering for larger enterprise contracts — it does add legal overhead and a small fee. For pilot sizing it's unusual but for multi-year commitments we can include escrow terms. We'll indicate the pathway in the redline.
[08:46] Jordan Lee: Competitors question — we've also been evaluating BigCloudAI. Pricing differences look like lower headline price but less flexibility on BYOK and less transparent latency profiles.
[08:59] Avery Chen: Yeah that's consistent — our differentiation is the Private & Dedicated posture plus observability and cost controls. We'll share performance artifacts relevant to your tokens per query distribution.
[09:13] Samir Gupta: For the latency sampling, can you instrument GPU tail latencies and cold-starts separately? We care about p95 and p99.
[09:22] Diego Ramos: Absolutely — we'll include p50/p95/p99 and cold/warm metrics. Also we'll surface batch size distributions.
[09:30] Maya Patel: Ok final check — SAML, SCIM, KMS BYOK for Private, 99.9% SLA for production, 12 month logs, export control redlines, escrow pathway if enterprise. Anything else?
[09:45] Avery Chen: Sounds complete. We'll produce three items: redline summary + pricing sheet (2026-02-20), Private deployment checklist + sampling plan (2026-02-21), and Notebook of KMS topology notes + your diagram (Samir 2026-02-23).
[10:02] Jordan Lee: Perfect. If we get those docs Tuesday, I can circulate to the committee for Thursday.
[10:09] Maya Patel: One more random transcribe quirk — the auto-transcript sometimes changed 'KV cache' to 'K-V cash' — just ignore.
[10:17] Diego Ramos: (laughs) noted.
[10:20] Avery Chen: Any outstanding blockers from security?
[10:24] Maya Patel: Not blockers — we have the export control clause and BYOK assurances as gating items. If the redline addresses those, security is comfortable to greenlight pilot.
[10:35] Samir Gupta: Also small ops ask — if you have a short runbook for rotating a key in the event of compromise, that would be helpful to include in the pilot docs.
[10:43] Diego Ramos: We'll add a concise key rotation/compromise runbook to the sampling doc.
[10:48] Jordan Lee: Cool — let's set the next call after you've sent the docs. I'm flexible Thursday afternoon for a quick 20–30 min readout.
[10:56] Avery Chen: We'll propose two slots for Thursday afternoon after docs are delivered. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in writing.
[11:05] (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (AE):
- Deliver redline summary + pricing by 2026-02-20 (Jordan needs for vendor committee)
- SE to prep Private VPC demo + latency sampling runbook (Diego, due 2026-02-21)
- Customer to provide KMS topology and key rotation policy (Samir, due 2026-02-23)
- Include escrow pathway mention for enterprise deals in redline packet
- Suggested pilot: 3-day evaluation with bounded fixed price, plus up to 2 benchmark runs (30–60m) instrumenting p50/p95/p99 and cold-starts.
